title: Machine learning links a plasma protein signature to symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection
summary: In the population-based Gutenberg COVID-19 Study, mass-spectrometry plasma proteomics of 494 post-infection and 190 pre-infection samples (paired samples from 189 participants) was analyzed with bootstrap mRMR ensemble feature selection and ridge regression, identifying 49 proteins associated with symptomatic rather than asymptomatic infection (10-fold cross-validated AUC 0.85). A score from the signature was associated with acute symptom burden, disease severity and post-COVID sequelae, and higher pre-infection HDL concentrations were inversely associated with it. The authors note that feature selection was performed outside the cross-validation folds, so discrimination may be optimistic, that the signature lacks external validation, and that post-COVID symptoms were self-reported.
ai_technology: Bootstrap mRMR ensemble feature selection with ridge regression builds a 49-protein score from plasma proteomics.
organization: University Medical Center of the Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz; Charité Universitätsmedizin Berlin; Institute of Molecular Biology (IMB), Mainz

evidence.tested: Signature evaluated by 10-fold cross-validation within one cohort; derived score tested for association with symptoms, severity and self-reported sequelae.
evidence.unknown: No external validation cohort; feature selection outside the cross-validation folds may inflate discrimination; mild infections were excluded from signature training; associations only.
evidence.ai_role: Ensemble feature selection and ridge regression identified the protein signature separating symptomatic from asymptomatic infection.

source_review.scope: Nature article HTML read: abstract, Methods (cohort, feature selection, ridge regression, nested cross-validation), limitations and publication dates; Europe PMC preprint search run.
